questions.stem: At what point must a Master, Limited candidate be at least 18 years old?
options: On the day they apply
On the day they receive the certificate
On the day they start sea service
On the day they pass the oral
questions.explanation: The age rule is at least 18 on the day the certificate is received. The sea service has to have been started after turning 16, which is the separate lower limit.

questions.stem: How much sea service does section 131 ask for if there is no approved on-board training program?
options: At least 6 months of deck duties
At least 1 month of deck duties
At least 2 months of deck duties
At least 12 months of deck duties
questions.explanation: Without an approved program the figure is at least 2 months. One month is the figure for service from an approved on-board training program.

questions.stem: Which sea service meets the 'same gross tonnage' condition for a certificate for a 30 GT vessel?
options: Service on any vessel of 10 GT or more
Service on vessels of any size so long as it is deck duty
Service only on the exact vessel named on the certificate
Service on vessels of 30 GT or more on matching voyage types
questions.explanation: The service has to be on vessels of at least the same GT as the vessel in question, on voyages like the certificate's. Smaller vessels do not count, and it need not be the same vessel, only one at least as large.

questions.stem: A candidate will run a 9 GT workboat that carries no passengers and has a VHF installed. Which item from the list is NOT required for this certificate?
options: A medical certificate
Marine basic first aid
A radio operator certificate
MED basic safety or a practical MED exam on the vessel's emergency equipment
questions.explanation: A medical certificate is required only when the certificate is for a passenger-carrying vessel. First aid, MED and the radio certificate (because VHF is fitted) all still apply.

questions.stem: What triggers the requirement for a radio operator certificate under section 131?
options: The vessel is over 15 GT
The vessel is equipped with a VHF radiotelephone installation
The vessel carries passengers
The vessel goes more than 5 nm offshore
questions.explanation: The condition in section 131 is that the vessel has a VHF radiotelephone installation. Size, passengers and distance offshore are not the trigger.

questions.stem: How early must the application documents be given to the examiner?
options: On the day of the first exam
At least 6 months before the first exam
At least 2 weeks before the first exam
Only after all exams are passed
questions.explanation: The documents go to the examiner at least two weeks before the first of the exams the applicant seeks to take. The application then stays valid for 1 year.

questions.stem: A candidate's MED course was completed 7 years before the application date. Which option meets the currency rule?
options: Nothing: the course is valid for life
A first aid certificate
3 months of service at any time in the last 5 years
12 months of deck service in the last 5 years, supported by a testimonial of competent participation in emergency drills
questions.explanation: A MED course should be within 5 years of the application. If it is older, accepted equivalents are a refresher in that period, 12 months of deck service in the last 5 years, or 3 months of deck service in the last 12 months, the service options being supported by a drills testimonial. 'Valid for life' applies after the certificate is issued and not to MED anyway.

questions.stem: Which of these correctly describes the MED requirement for a passenger-carrying vessel?
options: There is a passenger route: for example MED small passenger vessel safety, or basic safety plus seasonal passenger courses
MED basic safety alone is always enough
No MED is needed if the vessel is under 15 GT
A practical exam on the vessel's emergency equipment is always accepted instead
questions.explanation: The passenger-carrying vessel list is different from the non-passenger list: small passenger vessel safety, or basic safety plus a seasonal passenger course, or the two seasonal courses. The practical exam on the vessel's own equipment is an option only for non-passenger vessels.

questions.stem: Which of these requirements applies whatever the vessel carries or is equipped with?
options: A medical certificate
Marine basic first aid
A radio operator certificate
MED small passenger vessel safety
questions.explanation: Marine basic first aid is required for every Master, Limited < 60 GT candidate. The medical certificate depends on the vessel carrying passengers, the radio certificate on a VHF being fitted, and the passenger MED course on the vessel being passenger-carrying.

questions.stem: Who counts as a 'qualified person' under the rules this lesson covers?
options: Anyone over 18
Anyone with a first aid certificate
A Canadian citizen or permanent resident
Anyone who has passed NS1
questions.explanation: A qualified person is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. The candidate must prove this before the certificate is issued.
